title: Women's Employment Law, 5714-1954
source_id: ס"ח תשי"ד, 154 (Sefer HaChukim 5714, p 154); Knesset IsraelLawID 2001135; Wikisource page 'חוק עבודת נשים'
verified_how: Knesset Open Data KNS_IsraelLaw record fetched 23 September 2026: IsraelLawID 2001135, Name 'חוק עבודת נשים, התשי"ד-1954', KnessetNum 2, PublicationDate 1954-08-12, ValidityStartDate 1954-08-12, LatestPublicationDate 2026-03-31, LawValidityDesc 'תקף', ValidityFinishDate null, LastUpdatedDate 2025-09-15. KNS_LawBinding returned 73 rows: 1 'החוק המקורי' with PageNumber '154' and 72 'מתקן' rows - the most heavily amended Act in this group. The Hebrew Wikisource page 'חוק עבודת נשים' prints 'חוק עבודת נשים, תשי"ד–1954', citation 'ס"ח תשי"ד, 154' with amendments through 'תשפ"ו, 563', page last edited 1 June 2026, and no repeal marker for the Act itself. The Wikisource text records that this Act repealed (בוטל, in its s 25) the Mandate-era Women's Employment Ordinance 1945 (פקודת העבדתן של נשים), confirming that the 1954 Knesset Law and not the Ordinance is the operative instrument. Wikisource also flags a temporary provision (הוראת שעה) in s 9(c)(2c) running 31 March 2026 to 31 March 2027, which matches the official LatestPublicationDate of 2026-03-31.
notes: This is the maternity/parental leave statute (חופשת לידה / תקופת לידה והורות): length of leave, the right to extend or shorten it, leave for the other parent, nursing-hour deductions from the working day, and the prohibition on dismissal during and after the leave. TWO things a human must check. (1) A temporary provision in s 9(c)(2c) is in force only from 31 March 2026 to 31 March 2027 - an encoding must carry that sunset. (2) This Act confers the RIGHT to leave; the maternity/parental ALLOWANCE that makes the leave paid (דמי לידה) is paid by the National Insurance Institute under the National Insurance Law [Consolidated Version], 5755-1995, which is not indexed here. Encoding this Act alone gives leave entitlement and dismissal protection, not the money. Note also that the dismissal-protection provisions straddle this topic and Termination/severance.
